analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. docs/developer/desktop-app.md (head lines 421-430) now says Autopilot model recommendations rank by per-chip 24h earnings (`by_chip`, `by_chip_window`, `chipEarnings`, `recommendedModels`), falling back to seven-day network totals. The rest of the file is the same content shifted by seven lines, and I found no other changes in the diff. docs/reference/desktop-control.md updates the date and says `GET /control/v1/network` relays `/v1/stats` unchanged, including `by_chip` rows.

The changes touch no code, authorization, attestation, encryption, key custody, or provider-coordinator wire behavior (TB-002, TB-011). They do not touch the cache-storage posture in T-041 or the sandbox and add-on boundaries in TB-012 and TB-013.

The only plausible concern is that chip-level earnings are public, unauthenticated aggregate data from `/v1/stats`. They are used only to rank which models a user picks, and the user still explicitly confirms the selection. The documented recommendation logic could in principle be manipulated by a malicious provider or consumer who inflates per-chip earnings (a minor economic-steering risk). The supplied text shows no concrete control weakened, and the renderer and coordinator implementations are not in the supplied evidence. The `/v1/stats` source and the renderer's input validation for `by_chip` are outside this PR's evidence. I recommend verifying them if the code lands in a separate change. No threat-model entries need updating from these doc edits.
